units.en: Brother held treasures like those of Sui and He, not yet brought to light in writing; I wished to gather his works into one collection—will it be done in time?
units.literal: Younger brother held the treasures of Sui and He, not yet reaching to illumine the various writings; I wished to gather them into one collection—do you know whether in haste this can be done?

units.zh: 今已成服，吾臨靈取常共飲杯，酌自釀酒，寧有仿像不？
units.en: Now in mourning dress, I approach the spirit and take the cup we often shared, pour wine I brewed myself—is there perhaps some likeness of you?
units.literal: Now mourning garments are complete; I approach the spirit and take the cup we often drank together, pour self-brewed wine—is there perhaps some likeness?

units.zh: 冤痛！
units.en: Wronged pain!
units.literal: Wronged pain!

units.zh: 冤痛！
units.en: Wronged pain!
units.literal: Wronged pain!

units.zh: 元嘉三十年，卒，時年三十九。
units.en: He died in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, at the age of thirty-nine.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia he died, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 僧謙卒後四旬而微終。
units.en: Wei died forty days after Sengqian.
units.literal: Forty days after Sengqian's death Wei ended.

units.zh: 遺令薄葬，不設轜旐鼓挽之屬，施五尺床，為靈二宿便毀。
units.en: His final instructions were for a simple burial, without funeral carts, banners, drums, or processions; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights before the spirit, destroy it.
units.literal: His final command was simple burial, not setting out funeral carts, banners, drums, or pulling teams; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights at the spirit, destroy it.

units.zh: 以嘗所彈琴置床上，何長史來，以琴與之。
units.en: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.
units.literal: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.

units.zh: 何長史者，偃也。
units.en: Chief Clerk He was He Yan.
units.literal: Chief Clerk He was Yan.

units.zh: 無子。
units.en: He left no sons.
units.literal: He had no sons.

units.zh: 家人遵之。
units.en: The family followed his instructions.
units.literal: The family followed this.

units.zh: 所著文集傳於世。
units.en: His collected writings circulated in the world.
units.literal: The collected writings he authored were transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「微棲志貞深，文行惇洽，生自華宗，身安隱素，足以賁茲丘園，惇是薄俗。
units.en: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, an edict read: "Wei dwelt with pure and deep intent, his literary conduct sincere and harmonious; born of a great clan, he lived at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and enrich this shallow age.
units.literal: When Shizu took the throne an edict said: "Wei dwelt with intent pure and deep, literary conduct sincere and harmonious, born from a splendid clan, personally at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and thicken this thin custom.

units.zh: 不幸蚤世，朕甚悼之。
units.en: He died untimely, and I deeply mourn him.
units.literal: Unfortunate early death—I deeply mourn him.

units.zh: 可追贈秘書監。」
units.en: Let him be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."
units.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."

units.zh: 史臣曰：燕太子吐一言，田先生吞舌而死；
units.en: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word, and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;
units.literal: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;

units.zh: 安邑令戒屠者，閔仲叔去而之沛。
units.en: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left for Pei.
units.literal: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left and went to Pei.

units.zh: 良由內懷耿介，峻節不可輕干。
units.en: Truly because inwardly they harbor upright integrity—lofty integrity cannot be lightly offended.
units.literal: Truly because inwardly they harbor upright integrity—lofty integrity cannot be lightly offended.

units.zh: 袁淑笑謔之間，而王微弔詞連牘，斯蓋好名之士，欲以身為珪璋，皦皦然使塵玷之累，不能加也。
units.en: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, Wang Wei produced condolence letters sheet after sheet—such men love fame and wish to make themselves jade regalia, bright and clear so that the stain of dust cannot touch them.
units.literal: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, Wang Wei's condolence words linked sheets—this is probably a man who loves fame, wishing to make his person jade regalia, bright and clear so that the burden of dust and stain cannot be added.

units.zh: 立南郡公義慶為臨川王。
units.en: The Duke of Nan Commandery, Yiqing, was established as Prince of Linchuan.
units.literal: The Duke of Nan Commandery, Yiqing, was established as Prince of Linchuan.

units.zh: 追封司徒道規為臨川王。
units.en: The late Minister over the Masses Dao Gui was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.
units.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed the late Minister of Works Dao Gui as Prince of Linchuan.

units.zh: 樞肆志尋覽，殆將周遍，乃喟然歎曰：「吾聞貴爵位者以巢、由為桎梏，愛山林者以伊、呂為管庫，束名實則芻芥柱下之言，翫清虛則糠秕席上之說，稽之篤論，亦各從其好也。
units.en: Shu read through them almost entirely and sighed: "I hear that men who prize office take Chao Fu and Xu You as shackles, and men who love the hills take Yi and Lü as storekeepers; those who bind name to fact treat Laozi as straw, and those who play at emptiness treat banquet talk as chaff. In earnest judgment each follows his own bent.
units.literal: Shu with full intent searched and read them, nearly covering all; he then sighed and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and title take Chao Fu and Xu You as fetters, and those who love mountains and forests take Yi and Lü as granary keepers; binding name and reality makes Laozi's words mere hay; playing with emptiness and purity makes seat-side doctrines mere chaff; checked against earnest discourse, each also follows his own preference.

units.zh: 鏡少與光祿大夫顏延之隣居，顏談議飲酒，喧呼不絕；
units.en: As a youth Jing lived beside household minister Yan Yanzhi; Yan held drinking debates that roared on without pause;
units.literal: Jing in youth lived next to household minister Yan Yanzhi; Yan would hold drinking debates, clamor and shouting without cease;

units.zh: 後延之於籬邊聞其與客語，取胡牀坐聽，辭義清玄，延之心服，謂賔客曰：「彼有人焉。」
units.en: Later Yanzhi overheard him speaking with guests beyond the fence, brought a folding stool to sit and listen, and found his words lucid and deep. Yanzhi was convinced and told his guests, "There is a man over there."
units.literal: Later Yanzhi heard him talking with guests beyond the fence, took a folding stool and sat to listen; his words were clear and profound, and Yanzhi was won over and said to his guests, "There is a man there."

units.zh: 由此不復酣呌。
units.en: After that he never again drank himself into a racket.
units.literal: From this he no longer got rowdy drunk.

units.zh: 高祖東征孫恩，季高義樂隨。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor marched east against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed him out of loyalty.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned east against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed out of righteousness.

units.zh: 元熙二年，宋王令書以為高祖第四子義康右將軍司馬。
units.en: In the second year of Yuanxi an order from the Prince of Song appointed him Major on the staff of Right General Yikang, the Founding Emperor's fourth son.
units.literal: In the second year of Yuanxi, an order from the Prince of Song appointed him Major on the staff of the Right General for the Founding Emperor's fourth son Yikang.

units.zh: 高祖世子為征虜將軍，恩以大府佐領中兵參軍，隨府轉中兵參軍。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor's heir was made General Who Pacifies Barbarians, En served as Central Army Adjutant on the grand headquarters staff, and when the headquarters moved he retained that post.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor's heir was General Who Pacifies Barbarians, En as grand headquarters aide served as Central Army Adjutant; when the headquarters transferred he became Central Army Adjutant.

units.zh: 入關迎桂陽公義真。
units.en: He entered the passes to meet the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen.
units.literal: He entered the passes to meet the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen.

units.zh: 隨振武將軍道規西討，虜桓仙客，克偃月壘，遂平江陵。
units.en: He followed General Who Quells Martiality Daogui on the western campaign, captured Huan Xianke, took Yanyue fortress, and pacified Jiangling.
units.literal: Following General Who Quells Martiality Daogui west on campaign, he captured Huan Xianke, took Yanyue fortress, and pacified Jiangling.

units.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，前軍將軍道憐留鎮東府，領屯兵。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor marched against Sima Xiuzhi, Vanguard Army General Daolian remained to guard the Eastern Palace and command the garrison troops.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Vanguard Army General Daolian remained to guard the Eastern Palace and command the garrison troops.

units.zh: 高祖謂季高曰：「此賊行破，應先傾其巢窟，令奔走之日，無所歸投，非卿莫能濟事。」
units.en: The Founding Emperor told Jigao, "These rebels are on the verge of collapse. We must first destroy their base, so that when they flee they have nowhere to go. No one but you can see this through."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said to Jigao: "These rebels will soon be broken. We should first overturn their nest and stronghold, so that on the day they flee they will have nowhere to turn. No one but you can accomplish this."

units.zh: 九年，高祖念季高之功，乃表曰：「孫季高嶺南之勳，已蒙褒贈。
units.en: In the ninth year, remembering Jigao's service, the Founding Emperor submitted a memorial: "Sun Jigao's exploits in the Lingnan region have already been honored with posthumous rewards.
units.literal: In the ninth year, the Founding Emperor, mindful of Jigao's merit, submitted a memorial saying: "Sun Jigao's achievements south of the Ling have already received honorable posthumous grants.

units.zh: 臣更思惟盧循稔惡一紀，據有全域。
units.en: Yet I further consider that Lu Xun had grown wicked over a full twelve-year cycle and held an entire region.
units.literal: Your subject further reflects that Lu Xun accumulated wickedness for a full twelve-year cycle and held an entire region.

units.zh: 若令根本未拔，投奔有所，招合餘燼，猶能為虞；
units.en: Had his base not been destroyed and he still had somewhere to flee, he could have rallied the remnants of his force and remained a threat;
units.literal: If his root and trunk had not been uprooted and he had had somewhere to flee, gathering the embers of his force, he could still have caused trouble;

units.zh: 縣師遠討，方勤廟筭。
units.en: and the court would have had to dispatch armies on distant campaigns and labor over strategy in the ancestral temple.
units.literal: the imperial army would have had to campaign far away, and the court would have been busy with strategy in the temple.

units.zh: 而季高汎海萬里，投命洪流，波激電邁，指日遄至，遂奄定南海，覆其巢窟，使循進退靡依，輕舟遠迸。
units.en: Instead Jigao crossed ten thousand li of open sea, staking his life on the raging waters; riding wind and wave he arrived within days, swiftly secured Nanhai, and destroyed their stronghold, leaving Xun with nowhere to turn and driving him to flee in light boats.
units.literal: But Jigao crossed ten thousand li of sea, risking his life in the surging flood; waves leaped and lightning flashed as he arrived within days, then swiftly secured Nanhai and overturned their nest, leaving Xun with nowhere to advance or retreat and forcing him to flee in light boats.

units.zh: 曾不旬月，妖凶殲殄。
units.en: In less than a month the rebel scourge was wiped out.
units.literal: In less than a full month, the demonic rebels were utterly destroyed.

units.zh: 蕩滌之功，實庸為大。
units.en: The merit of clearing them away was truly great.
units.literal: The merit of sweeping them away was truly great.

units.zh: 往年所贈，猶為未優。
units.en: The rewards granted in earlier years were still inadequate.
units.literal: What was granted in previous years was still insufficient.

units.zh: 愚謂宜更贈一州，即其本號，庶令忠勳不湮，勞臣增厲。」
units.en: I humbly submit that one further prefecture should be granted posthumously under his former title, so that loyal service may not be forgotten and hardworking ministers may be further inspired."
units.literal: I humbly propose that one further prefecture be granted posthumously, bearing his former title, so that loyal merit may not be lost and laboring ministers may be further encouraged."

units.zh: 將向京邑，高祖命曰：「預是彭、沛鄉人赴義者，並可依劉主簿。」
units.en: As they prepared to march on the capital, the Founding Emperor ordered, "All men of Peng and Pei who have risen in the cause may report to Chief Clerk Liu."
units.literal: When about to march on the capital region, the Founding Emperor ordered: "All who from Peng and Pei country have come out in righteousness may attach themselves to Chief Clerk Liu."

units.zh: 明日，桓謙屯於東陵，卞範之屯覆舟山西，高祖疑賊有伏兵，顧視左右，正見鍾，謂之曰：「此山下當有伏兵，卿可率部下稍往撲之。」
units.en: The next day Huan Qian encamped at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou mountain. Suspecting an ambush, the Founding Emperor looked about and spotted Zhong. "There are likely hidden troops on this hillside," he said. "Take your men forward and flush them out."
units.literal: The next day Huan Qian encamped at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi at west of Fuzhou mountain. The Founding Emperor suspected the enemy had hidden troops; looking left and right, he saw Zhong and said to him: "There ought to be hidden troops below this mountain. You may lead your subordinates a little ways forward to flush them out."

units.zh: 高祖平定京邑，以為振武將軍，封新夷縣五等侯。
units.en: After the Founding Emperor secured the capital, he appointed Sun Chu General Who Quells Martiality and enfeoffed him as a fifth-rank marquis of Xin'yi county.
units.literal: After the Founding Emperor pacified the capital region, he made him General Who Quells Martiality and enfeoffed him as a five-rank marquis of Xin'yi county.

units.zh: 高祖征孫恩，縣差為征民，充乙士，使伐馬芻。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor marched against Sun En, the county drafted him for the campaign as a second-class soldier and set him to cutting horse fodder.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Sun En, the county conscripted him as campaign labor, assigning him as a second-class soldier to cut horse fodder.

units.zh: 高祖聞之，即給器仗，恩大喜。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor heard this, he immediately gave En weapons and armor, and En was overjoyed.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor heard this, he immediately gave him weapons and armor; En was greatly delighted.

units.zh: 高祖西征劉毅，恩與王鎮惡輕軍襲江陵，事在鎮惡傳。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor marched west against Liu Yi, En and Wang Zhen'e led light troops in a surprise attack on Jiangling— the full account appears in Zhen'e's biography.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned west against Liu Yi, En with Wang Zhen'e led light troops in a surprise attack on Jiangling; the account is in Zhen'e's biography.

units.zh: 高祖伐司馬休之及魯宗之，恩與建威將軍徐逵之前進。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, En advanced with General Who Establishes Might Xu Dazhi.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, En advanced together with General Who Establishes Might Xu Dazhi.

units.zh: 高祖善其能將軍持重。
units.en: The Founding Emperor praised his ability to hold an army steady under pressure.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor praised his ability to command the army with weight and steadiness.

units.zh: 高祖錄其前後功勞，封新寧縣男，食邑五百戶。
units.en: The Founding Emperor recorded his accumulated service and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xining county with a fief of five hundred households.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor recorded his merits before and after and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xining county with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 高祖北伐，留恩侍衛世子，命朝士與之交。
units.en: On the Founding Emperor's northern campaign En was left to guard the heir, and was instructed to keep company with court gentlemen.
units.literal: On the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, En was left to guard the heir; he was ordered to associate with court gentlemen.

units.zh: 隆安四年，高祖伐孫恩，鍾願從餘姚、浹口攻句章、海鹽、婁縣，皆摧堅陷陣，每有戰功。
units.en: In the fourth year of Long'an the Founding Emperor marched against Sun En; Zhong volunteered and fought at Juzhang, Haiyan, and Lou county from Yuyao and Jiakou, breaking through every strong position and winning merit in every engagement.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, the Founding Emperor attacked Sun En; Zhong volunteered to follow, attacking Juzhang, Haiyan, and Lou county from Yuyao and Jiakou—all smashing hard positions and breaking formations, with merit in every battle.

units.zh: 高祖每有戎事，鍾不辭艱劇，專心盡力，甚見愛信。
units.en: Whenever the Founding Emperor took the field, Zhong never shrank from hardship, giving himself wholly to the task, and won great trust and favor.
units.literal: Whenever the Founding Emperor had military affairs, Zhong never declined hardship and toil, devoting heart and strength; he was greatly trusted and favored.

units.zh: 義旗將建，高祖版鍾為郡主簿。
units.en: As the righteous banner was about to be raised, the Founding Emperor commissioned Zhong chief clerk of the commandery.
units.literal: As the righteous banner was about to be raised, the Founding Emperor issued Zhong a commission as chief clerk of the commandery.

units.zh: 於是立為義隊，恆在左右，連戰皆捷。
units.en: A volunteer unit was formed with Zhong always at the Founding Emperor's side, and battle after battle was won.
units.literal: Thereupon a righteous-force unit was formed with Zhong always at his side; battle after battle was victorious.

units.zh: 桓玄西奔，其夕，高祖止桓謙故營，遣鍾宿據東府，轉鎮軍參軍督護。
units.en: Huan Xuan fled west; that evening the Founding Emperor camped at Huan Qian's former position and sent Zhong to hold the Eastern Palace. Zhong was then made Inspector-and-Protector on the Army Pacification General's staff.
units.literal: Huan Xuan fled west; that evening the Founding Emperor halted at Huan Qian's former camp and sent Zhong to garrison the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to Inspector-and-Protector under the Army Pacification General.

units.zh: 桓歆寇歷陽，遣鍾助豫州刺史魏詠之討之，歆即奔迸。
units.en: When Huan Xin raided Liyang, the Founding Emperor sent Zhong to assist Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Yongzhi; Xin fled at once.
units.literal: Huan Xin raided Liyang; he sent Zhong to assist Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Yongzhi to attack him; Xin at once fled in panic.

units.zh: 自陳情事，改葬父祖及親屬十喪，高祖厚加資給。
units.en: He petitioned to reinter his father, grandfather, and ten other relatives; the Founding Emperor generously provided the funds.
units.literal: He stated his personal circumstances: reburial of his father, grandfather, and ten relatives' funerals; the Founding Emperor generously provided funds.

units.zh: 高祖討劉毅，鍾率軍繼王鎮惡。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor marched against Liu Yi, Zhong led an army in support of Wang Zhen'e.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Liu Yi, Zhong led troops following Wang Zhen'e.

units.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，復留鎮居守，增其兵力，又命府置佐史。
units.en: In the twelfth year, when the Founding Emperor marched north, Zhong was again left to guard the capital; his forces were increased, and he was ordered to appoint staff assistants and clerks for his headquarters.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, on the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, Zhong was again left to guard the capital; his military strength was increased, and he was ordered to appoint staff assistants and clerks for his headquarters.

units.zh: 荊州刺史道憐獻名馬三匹，并精麗乘具，高祖悉以賜鍾三子。
units.en: Inspector of Jingzhou Daolian presented three famous horses with fine harness and riding gear, and the Founding Emperor gave them all to Zhong's three sons.
units.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Daolian presented three famous horses together with fine harness and riding gear; the Founding Emperor gave them all to Zhong's three sons.

units.zh: 隆安中，從高祖征孫恩，戍句章城，被圍數十日，無日不戰，身被數創。
units.en: During Long'an he followed the Founding Emperor against Sun En, garrisoned Juzhang, and was besieged for several tens of days; he fought every day and suffered several wounds.
units.literal: During Long'an he followed the Founding Emperor against Sun En, garrisoned Juzhang city, was besieged for several tens of days, fought every day without exception, and suffered several wounds.

units.zh: 元興元年，又從高祖東征臨海，於石步固與盧循相守二十餘日。
units.en: In the first year of Yuanxing he again followed the Founding Emperor east against Linhai and at Shibu fortress held Lu Xun at bay for more than twenty days.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing he again followed the Founding Emperor east against Linhai and at Shibu fortress faced Lu Xun for more than twenty days.

units.zh: 二年，又從高祖至東陽，破徐道覆。
units.en: In the second year he again followed the Founding Emperor to Dongyang and defeated Xu Daofu.
units.literal: In the second year he again followed the Founding Emperor to Dongyang and defeated Xu Daofu.

units.zh: 從高祖伐廣固，於臨朐破賊。
units.en: He joined the Founding Emperor's campaign against Guanggu and routed the enemy at Linqu.
units.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor in the campaign against Guanggu and defeated the rebels at Linqu.

units.zh: 盧循逼京邑，孟昶、諸葛長民等建議奉天子過江，進廷議不可，面折昶等，高祖甚嘉之。
units.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed moving the emperor south across the Yangzi. Qiujin argued before the court that this was unacceptable and openly refuted Chang and his allies; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.
units.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed escorting the Son of Heaven across the river; Jin argued in court that this was unacceptable and rebutted Chang and the others to their faces. The Founding Emperor greatly praised him.

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 年二十，遭王莽敗，世祖即位於冀州。
units.en: At twenty he lived through Wang Mang's fall and watched Liu Xiu raise the Han banner in Ji.
units.literal: At twenty he encountered Wang Mang's collapse, and the Founding Ancestor took the throne in Ji Province.

units.zh: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之：「我何如君亡叔？」
units.en: When Huan Xuan became Grand Commandant, the whole court assembled. He asked Zhenzhi, "How do I compare with your late uncle?"
units.literal: When Huan Xuan was Grand Commandant, court ministers all gathered; asked Zhenzhi, "How am I compared to your lord's deceased uncle?"

units.zh: 楨之曰：「亡叔一時之標，公是千載之英。」
units.en: Zhenzhi answered, "My uncle was the paragon of his age; you are a hero for the ages."
units.literal: Zhenzhi said, "Deceased uncle was one generation's standard; you lord are a thousand generations' hero."

units.zh: 好讀《太玄經》，註揚雄《蜀都賦》。
units.en: He loved to read the Classic of Supreme Mystery and annotated Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Capital of Shu.
units.literal: He loved to read the Classic of Supreme Mystery and annotated Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Capital of Shu.

units.zh: 每云：「我欲與揚子雲周旋。」
units.en: He would often say, "I wish to keep company with Yang Ziyun."
units.literal: He would often say, "I wish to keep company with Yang Ziyun."

units.zh: 昔燕太子使荆轲劫始皇，变起两楹之间，其后谒者持匕首刺腋，高祖偃武行文，故易之以板。」
units.en: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward receptionists carried daggers at the armpit. Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced them with tablets."
units.literal: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward a receptionist stabbed him in the armpit with a dagger. Emperor Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced daggers with tablets."

units.zh: 蜀丞相诸葛亮问广汉秦密，董扶及任安所长。
units.en: Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang asked the Guanghan scholar Qin Mi what Dong Fu and Ren An respectively excelled at.
units.literal: The Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi of Guanghan what Dong Fu and Ren An were each good at.

units.zh: 淑及徐湛之、江湛、王僧綽、卜天與四家，於是長給稟祿。
units.en: The four households of Shu, Xu Zhizhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo, and Bu Tianyu thereafter received permanent stipends.
units.literal: For the four households of Shu, Xu Zhizhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo, and Bu Tianyu, permanent stipends were thereafter granted.

units.zh: 世祖即位，使顏延之為詔曰：「夫輕道重義，亟聞其教；世弊國危，希遇其人。自非達義之至，識正之深者，孰能抗心衞主，遺身固節者哉。故太子左衞率淑，文辯優洽，秉尚貞慤。當要逼之切，意色不橈，厲辭道逆，氣震凶黨。虐刃交至，取斃不移。古之懷忠隕難，未云出其右者。興言嗟悼，無廢乎心。宜在加禮，永旌宋有臣焉。可贈侍中、太尉，諡曰忠憲公。」
units.en: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he had Yan Yanzhi draft an edict: "When the Way is slighted and righteousness weighed heavily, the teaching has long been heard; in an age of decay and a state in peril, such a person is rarely met. Unless one has reached the utmost in grasping righteousness and depth in knowing what is correct, who could brace the heart to guard his lord, leave the body, and hold fast to integrity? Former Left Guard General of the Heir Apparent Shu was eloquent and thorough and upheld pure sincerity. When coercion pressed hardest, his expression did not bend; with stern words he denounced rebellion, and his spirit shook the vicious faction. Cruel blades fell together, yet he met death without wavering. Among the loyal who fell in disaster in antiquity, none are said to surpass him. At these words we sigh and mourn, and our hearts cannot be unmoved. He deserves added honors, eternally displaying that Song had such a minister. He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Integrity."
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he had Yan Yanzhi draft an edict saying: "When the Way is slighted and righteousness weighed heavily, the teaching has long been heard; in an age of decay and a state in peril, such a person is rarely met. Unless one has reached the utmost in grasping righteousness and depth in knowing what is correct, who could brace the heart to guard his lord, leave the body, and hold fast to integrity? Former Left Guard General of the Heir Apparent Shu was eloquent and thorough in discourse and upheld pure sincerity. When coercion pressed hardest, his expression did not bend; with stern words he denounced rebellion, and his spirit shook the vicious faction. Cruel blades fell together, yet he met death without wavering. Among ancient men who cherished loyalty and fell in disaster, none are said to surpass him. At these words we sigh and mourn, and our hearts cannot be unmoved. He deserves added honors, eternally displaying that Song had such a minister. He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Integrity."

units.zh: 五世祖湛，宋左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，忠簡公。
units.en: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan had been Song's left grand master of the palace and a grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices, posthumously titled the loyal and simple duke.
units.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan was Song Left Grand Master of the Palace, Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, the loyal and simple Duke.

units.zh: 見嵇康《養生論》，自是歷代未有天下通用如趙過一畝三甽之法者。
units.en: See Ji Kang's Treatise on Nourishing Life; no method since has been applied empire-wide like Zhao Guo's three-furrow-per-mu system.
units.literal: See Ji Kang's "Treatise on Nourishing Life"; from then on through successive dynasties none was universally applied under heaven like Zhao Guo's method of three furrows per mu.

units.zh: 庚午，以司空道憐為太尉，封長沙王。
units.en: On the day gengwu, the Minister of Works Dao Lin was appointed Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.
units.literal: On the day gengwu, the Minister of Works Dao Lin was made Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.

units.zh: 太尉長沙王道憐、司空徐羨之、尚書僕射傅亮、領軍將軍謝晦、護軍將軍檀道濟並入侍醫藥。
units.en: Grand Marshal Prince of Changsha Dao Lin, Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Secretariat Director Fu Liang, Commander-in-Chief Xie Hui, and Protector General Tan Daoji all entered to attend him with medicine.
units.literal: Grand Marshal Prince of Changsha Dao Lin, Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Secretariat Director Fu Liang, Commander-in-Chief Xie Hui, and Protector General Tan Daoji all entered to attend medicine.

units.zh: 太尉持節監護，葬以晉禮。
units.en: The Grand Commandant held imperial credentials to oversee the funeral, and burial followed Jin rites.
units.literal: The Grand Commandant held imperial credentials to oversee the funeral, and burial followed Jin rites.

units.zh: 宋大明用江夏王義恭，以後無人。
units.en: Song's Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held it in the Daming era; after that, no one.
units.literal: In Song's Daming era Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held it; afterward no one.

units.zh: 太宰。
units.en: Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 上與荊州刺史衡陽王義季書曰：「殷僕射疾患少日，奄忽不救。
units.en: The emperor wrote to Prince Hengyang Yiji, governor of Jingzhou: "Vice Director Yin was ill only a few days and then was suddenly beyond help.
units.literal: The Emperor wrote to Prince Hengyang Yiji, Governor of Jingzhou: "Vice Director Yin was ill only a few days and suddenly could not be saved.

units.zh: 《宋書·止足傳》有羊欣、王微，咸其流亞。
units.en: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.
units.literal: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.

units.zh: 又分荊州十郡還立湘州，左衞將軍張邵為湘州刺史。
units.en: Also ten commanderies of Jing Province were separated to re-establish Xiang Province; Left Guards General Zhang Shao was made Governor of Xiang Province.
units.literal: Also ten commanderies of Jing Province were separated to re-establish Xiang Province; Left Guards General Zhang Shao was made Governor of Xiang Province.
